data.why: The repository ships its own Excel workbook (DATA_ Daily_CGWB_Stations_2022-2025.xlsx) with all six station sheets the app loads by default; no uploads or synthetic data are needed.

goals: Compare rainfall and evaporation trends across the six Hyderabad groundwater monitoring stations to see which are under deficit vs. surplus
Inspect the cumulative net water balance curve for a station to identify monsoon recharge periods versus dry-season depletion
Generate a zero-shot TimesFM forecast for a chosen variable (e.g. net water balance) and horizon at a station, and judge its skill against seasonal and persistence baselines
Decide whether the validation-weighted ensemble or a single method gives the most trustworthy near-term forecast for a given station/variable
Cross-check the station's historical forecast with the live 10-day ECMWF weather forecast to reason about near-term recharge potential

review.summary: The surveying, historical-hydrology and weather parts of this tree are accurate, at the right depth, and fully supported by the screens I checked. The tool's main purpose, TimesFM forecasting judged against baselines with a validation-weighted ensemble, is absent because the model download never finished, so the tree needs that phase re-run or added as blocked nodes before filing.
